newsitem.title: FRANCE: Arthuis says has German support on EMU council.
newsitem.headline: Arthuis says has German support on EMU council.

text.p: France will push ahead in the next few months to win backing for a stability council to act as a counterweight to the European Central Bank after the launch of monetary union, Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said on Thursday.
The proposal had not yet won majority support in the European Union, he said.
"But I can assure you that our way of seeing things is totally shared by our German partners," he told a conference on the new euro currency.
"I plan to work in the next few months to widen support for this idea," he said. "It is very important that there is a political pillar to act as a counterweight in the institutional balance."
Some politicians have voiced fears that the future European Central Bank -- modelled on the independent German Bundesbank -- will exert too much power after the launch of a single currency.
In response France has proposed a "stability council" -- which could be criticised by some as a form of embryonic government -- that will co-ordinate economic policies after monetary union.
